title: Trust in the Lord fully — Proverbs 3
paragraphs: Trust in the Lord fully — Proverbs 3
You say you trust God.
But your anxiety tells another story.

You plan every outcome.
Control every detail.
Lose sleep over things you can’t carry.
And still say, “Lord, I trust You.”
Do you?

“Trust in the Lord with all your heart
and lean not on your own understanding…” — Proverbs 3:5
All your heart.

Not half.
Not when it’s convenient.
Not only when the outcome looks safe.
All.
But here’s what we miss…

Trust is not a feeling.
It’s surrender.

It’s choosing God’s wisdom when yours feels louder.
It’s walking forward when the path is unclear.
It’s letting go of control—even when your hands are shaking.
Because the truth?

Our understanding is limited.
Broken by sin.
Blurred by fear.
But God sees the end from the beginning.
And that’s where grace walks in.

Because Jesus didn’t just tell us to trust—
He modeled it.

In the garden, facing the cross, He prayed:
“Not My will, but Yours be done.” (Luke 22:42)
That’s trust.
Bloody. Costly. Real.
And through that surrender, He secured your salvation.

So now, when you trust God,
you’re not falling into the unknown—

you’re falling into the hands of a Savior
who already proved His love on the cross.
He can be trusted.

Even when life doesn’t make sense.
Even when prayers feel unanswered.
Even when the road hurts.
So today—
Stop leaning on your own understanding.
Release it.
All of it.
And trust the One who never fails.
From control to Christ—because Jesus rewrites everything.
